title: Warfarin Therapy and VKORC1 and CYP Genotype
journal: Medical Genetics Summaries, National Center for Biotechnology Information (US)
result: Peer-reviewed chapter, first posted 8 March 2012, version 4.0 of 16 June 2026. VKORC1, on chromosome 16p11.2, encodes vitamin K epoxide reductase, which catalyses the rate-limiting step of vitamin K recycling and is the target of warfarin. The promoter variant c.-1639G>A (rs9923231) is associated with lower protein expression, increased warfarin sensitivity and lower dose requirements; the variant allele is the major allele (about 90%) in Asian populations and has a frequency of about 40% in people of European descent and 14% in African Americans. VKORC1 accounts for about 30% of the variation in dose requirement, CYP2C9 usually for less than 10%.
